title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Wall Street opens the week still shaking off Friday's AI-driven selloff (S&P 500 -1.8%, Nasdaq -2.9%, its worst day since June); Nasdaq remains roughly 8% below its October record high.

Markets: Fed December rate-hike odds have slipped to ~69% (from ~85% right after last week's hold at 3.75%-4.00%) as the tech rout eases pressure on policymakers; the 10-year Treasury yield sits near 4.93%.

Companies: Alphabet sank ~12% on its Q3 report and Amazon slipped despite AWS revenue surging 39% and a record 13.9% operating margin — investors remain fixated on rising AI capex over the earnings beats.
Companies: Binance's $6.3B hack, tied to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, stands as the largest crypto heist on record; Coinbase shares remain pressured with no confirmed recovery of funds.
Macro/Policy: Investors are bracing for Tuesday's US midterm elections, with markets broadly favoring a divided Congress as the most market-friendly outcome.
Macro/Policy: A bipartisan energy-permitting bill is hitting Democratic resistance over fears it favors a natural-gas buildout over renewables amid AI-driven power demand.
